Київ, атака ввечері 13 жовтня й уночі 14: Kyiv, attack on the evening of 13 October and overnight into 14 October. The first missile wave at about 23:00 hit a nine-storey apartment building in Desnianskyi district, where, according to the State Emergency Service, at least two people had been killed and more than 20 injured at the time of the first report, and 16 residents were evacuated; the fire spread through flats from the first to the eighth floor. According to the Kyiv City Prosecutor’s Office (via Ukrinform, 08:50), three women were killed in Desnianskyi district and one more person in Holosiivskyi district (a non-residential building), i.e. 4 killed and 27 injured; according to Suspilne Kyiv (08:37, citing the military administration, the State Emergency Service and police), 3 killed and 32 injured, 2 killed and 25 injured of them in Desnianskyi district. The discrepancy comes from different timing and counting methods; there are no final figures. Rescue work was continuing in the morning; criminal proceedings have been opened under Art. 438 of the Criminal Code (war crimes). Private houses and apartment buildings, cars, an office building, a café, a library, a stadium and a school were also damaged. No day of mourning was declared (not mentioned in the sources).

Київ, ТЕЦ-4 і житловий будинок, 13–14 жо: Kyiv, CHP-4 and an apartment building, 13–14 October. The first missile wave at about 22:30–23:00 hit CHP-4 (according to Zelensky, one of the city’s main combined heat and power plants) and a nine-storey building in Desnianskyi district; the second series began after 04:00 and lasted several hours (according to the Kyiv Independent, explosions between 04:45 and 06:45). Fires broke out in Dniprovskyi, Darnytskyi and Shevchenkivskyi districts; DTEK introduced emergency outages in five districts, and trams and trolleybuses stopped in part of the city. According to Zelensky, at least 600,000 people in the country are without power, 26 elements of the energy system and four oil and gas facilities were damaged; the strike targeted the energy systems of Kyiv, Kyiv region and Kharkiv. Kyiv and the Air Force say partners did not pass on information about ballistic launches on either 12.10 or 13.10: the missiles were detected by radar only near the city, and the reasons are being investigated. Zelensky called the strike a “demonstrative disrespect” for the United States after the “energy ceasefire” announced by Trump and called for sanctions under Senator Lindsey Graham’s bill and additional Patriot systems. The Air Force clarified that partners had not given warning before each wave (Glavcom, 09:58).

Москва і область, ніч на 14 жовтня. За м: Moscow and the region, night of 14 October. According to Mayor Sergei Sobyanin (via RBC-Ukraine, 08:33), from 20:30 on 13.10 to 07:00 on 14.10, 493 drones flew towards the Moscow region, and another 180 were shot down closer to the capital; there were about ten waves, and TASS called it one of the largest attacks in two years (claimed by russia). Sheremetyevo, Domodedovo, Vnukovo and Zhukovsky temporarily suspended operations, Vnukovo was closed for more than eight hours; Zn.ua reports more than 400 cancelled and delayed flights. The local authorities effectively confirmed a massive attack and airport disruption, but did not name any sites hit or report casualties. As of the morning of 14.10 the General Staff, SBU, HUR, SSO and USF had not confirmed the strike, and the targets are unknown, so this is only an indirect sign of its scale.

Трамп призупинив «пекельні санкції» за з: Trump suspended the “hellish sanctions” under the Graham law two days before they were due to start. By an executive order of 16 October Trump formally imposed, but immediately suspended, 100% tariffs on goods from the largest buyers of russian oil and gas and 500% tariffs on russian energy under the “Lindsey Graham Sanctioning russia and Iran Act of 2026”, which he himself signed on 18 September. The stated basis is a certification to Congress that waiving them “at this stage” is in the US national interest; the tariffs were to take effect after 18 October. The order does not lift previously imposed sanctions, and the suspension has no set end date. Санкції за «законом Грема». Указом від п: Sanctions under the “Graham law”. By an executive order of Friday, 16 October, implementing the “Lindsey Graham Sanctioning russia and Iran Act of 2026” (Trump signed it on 18 September), the US president formally imposed and then immediately suspended 100% tariffs on goods from the largest buyers of russian oil and gas, 500% tariffs on russian energy and sanctions on a number of russian entities. The legal basis is section 115 of the act, which allows the president to waive the measures subject to a written certification to Congress that this is in the US national interest. The suspension remains in force until Trump or the Secretary of State decides otherwise; the order does not touch previously imposed sanctions. Ukrinform (06:33 17.10) and Newsweek link the decision to Trump’s diesel deal with Putin of 9 October; the order itself does not mention diesel, and the White House has not confirmed a causal link. According to Ukrinform, 12 senators from both parties this week urged Trump to cancel the deal with Putin and enforce the law; Republican congressman Michael McCaul called the intention to lower diesel prices understandable but warned that easing pressure on russian oil would “only fund the Kremlin’s war machine”. Experts cited by Novaya Gazeta Europe consider the law largely symbolic, but the first significant increase in pressure on the kremlin during Trump’s term.

Sanctions under the “Graham law”: a new detail. Secretary of State Marco Rubio on 18 October (according to the Kyiv Independent) described the suspension of tariffs and sanctions, which Trump formalised by executive order on 16.10, as a 60-day period to analyse the effects of imposing sanctions and tariffs simultaneously, citing high global energy prices due to the US war with Iran. Earlier, according to the text of the order (Ukrinform, Newsweek), the suspension had no set term, lasting until the president or the secretary of state decide otherwise — see “discrepancies”. Reaction: according to headlines in Axios (17.10), the Washington Post and CNN, the decision drew instant bipartisan criticism in Congress; Zelensky, according to a CNBC headline, called it “wrong”. kremlin special envoy Kirill Dmitriev called it a “historic moment” (see “What they say in the swamps”).

Starlink. За Axios, 17 жовтня Зеленський: Starlink. According to Axios, on 17 October Zelensky said that Starlink use in Ukraine remains partly restricted: military tests on Friday showed that a connected vehicle kept its link at 180 km/h in EU countries, while in Ukraine the signal dropped at 161 km/h; he called it a “planned operation”. The restrictions prevent using drones to intercept russian drones and supplying troops. According to Reuters (15.10, anonymous US and Western officials), the order to slow Starshield came from inside the White House; the White House and Trump (16.10) deny involvement, and The Telegraph writes that Musk proposed the restrictions to Trump — the White House called this “totally false”. Ukraine’s chief negotiator Rustem Umerov discussed it with Jared Kushner on Friday; according to Axios, they also talked about a meeting of the US and Ukrainian teams planned for next week on Trump’s proposal to end the war.
Заморожені російські активи. Відповідаюч: Frozen russian assets. Answering journalists’ questions on 17 October (according to Obozrevatel), Zelensky said Kyiv has information about russia’s attempts, through certain partners, to recover or unfreeze part of the frozen assets, but all details have been discussed with the Europeans, and the issue is now “under Europe’s full control”.
Втрати у війні. Відповідаючи на запитанн: War losses. Answering journalists’ questions on Friday 16 October (according to Ukrinform, 17.10; location not given), Trump repeated that he knows the “details” of the war and will one day make them public, that he is interested only in ending the war, and said that on average about 25,000 soldiers a month die in it, and last month 32,000. He did not say where the figures come from or whether they cover both sides’ losses. For comparison, Ukraine’s General Staff claims 46,230 russian losses (killed and wounded combined) for September — not independently verified.

Віткофф везе Путіну оновлену мирну пропо: Witkoff takes an updated peace proposal to Putin after talks with Zelensky in Oslo
21 жовтня спецпосланець 🇺🇸 США Стів Вітк: US special envoy Steve Witkoff is meeting Putin in Saint Petersburg on 21 October — in the first half of the day, according to Putin’s foreign-policy aide Yuri Ushakov (as retold by Vedomosti citing RIA Novosti). The day before, in Oslo, Witkoff met Zelensky, the leaders of Finland and Norway and representatives of other European governments; Jared Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law and informal envoy, joined online (Kyiv Independent, Axios). They discussed a “framework agreement” and security guarantees modelled on NATO’s Article 5. Zelensky wants the next step to be a three-way meeting of leaders — something russia has so far refused. The claims of “meaningful progress”, and that Kushner pressed Kyiv to stop striking russian oil refineries, come only from an unnamed US official quoted by Axios; there is no official readout from Oslo, no text of the proposal, and no outcome of the Putin meeting as of this morning. The same night russia launched 186 drones and Iskander-K cruise missiles at Ukraine.
Віткофф везе Путіну оновлену мирну пропо: As Steve Witkoff heads into a meeting with Putin in Saint Petersburg carrying an updated US peace proposal, russia sent 186 drones at Ukraine overnight, and fighting along the front rose by a third in a day. The proposal follows talks in Oslo with Zelensky and European leaders; the only account of “meaningful progress” — and of US pressure on Kyiv to stop hitting russian refineries — comes from an unnamed US official speaking to Axios.
Цивільні жертви російських ударів за 20: Civilians killed and injured by russian strikes on 20 October and overnight into the 21st, as reported by the authorities by the morning of 21 October, including updated figures for the strike of 19 October. Figures are incomplete and may rise:
Нова Водолага (Харківщина), удар по парк: Nova Vodolaha, a small town about 45 km south-west of Kharkiv: update on the strike on a park on the evening of 19 October. Six people were killed and 15 injured, according to Kharkiv’s regional governor Oleh Syniehubov (via Ukrinform, 19.10 18:36); police say a Geran-3 drone — russia’s version of the Iranian Shahed — was used. Sources differ on how many of the dead were children: Ukrinform says three, Censor.NET, citing the regional administration (20.10 09:59), says two girls, aged 1 and 11; seven of the injured were children, per Censor.NET. The discrepancy has not been officially explained.
Київщина та Дніпро, 20 жовтня. У Чабанах: Kyiv region and Dnipro, 20 October. In Chabany, just outside Kyiv, a drone hit the Kyiv–Odesa highway and set cars on fire: three dead, four injured; prosecutors have opened a war-crimes case (Kyiv region prosecutor’s office). In the suburbs of Dnipro, at about 8:40, russia struck warehouses: two dead and four injured, three of them with severe burns (Oleksandr Hanzha, Dnipropetrovsk regional authorities). The reports we read do not say what weapons were used in either case.
269 бойових зіткнень за 20 жовтня — на т: 269 combat clashes on 20 October — a third more than the day before (206, per an Ukrinform headline), according to Ukraine’s General Staff as of 08:00 on 21 October. The heaviest assaults were around Kostiantynivka (37) and Pokrovsk (30), the two towns at the centre of russia’s push in Donetsk region. russia carried out 86 air strikes with 302 KAB glide bombs, used 9,757 kamikaze drones and shelled Ukrainian positions and towns 2,735 times (13 times with multiple rocket launchers). Only 123 of the 269 assaults are broken down by direction; another 3 air strikes (6 KABs) and 53 shellings fell on the North Slobozhanskyi and Kursk directions, where no assaults were recorded. 186 ударних дронів за ніч на 21 жовтня —: 186 attack drones overnight into 21 October — more than the night before (165), but below the average of the previous seven nights (≈264, pulled up by the mass attack of 15 October, when 582 were launched). Ukraine’s Air Force says 150 were shot down or jammed by 08:30 — 81%, up from 70% the night before (115 of 165); 10 were still in the air; hits were recorded at 27 locations and falling debris at 13. Among the drones were 88 jet-powered Shaheds (63 of them downed); “Banderol” S-8000/Dan-T, “Gerbera” decoys and “Parodiya” drones were not counted separately. russia also fired Iskander-K cruise missiles from the airspace over Rostov region; the report does not say how many. The drones were launched from around Oryol, Kursk and Primorsko-Akhtarsk in russia, from occupied Hvardiiske in Donetsk region and from Chauda in occupied Crimea. The figures for the night of 20 October come from an Ukrinform headline; the article itself was not read.

Осло — Санкт-Петербург. 20 жовтня в 🇳🇴 О: From Oslo to Saint Petersburg. On 20 October in Oslo, US special envoy Steve Witkoff met Zelensky, Norway’s prime minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Finland’s president Alexander Stubb; Jared Kushner joined online, and talks with European national security advisers were to follow (Kyiv Independent). Zelensky said Ukraine and its partners want the US to pass their ideas on to russia, and proposed a three-way meeting of leaders as the next step. Støre said the Saint Petersburg talks “could open the way” to a leaders’ meeting; Stubb said the sides had found “key elements” on security and the economy. The rest comes from an unnamed US official quoted by Axios (Barak Ravid, 20.10 23:04 UTC): the sides made “meaningful progress”; on Wednesday Witkoff will present Putin with an updated proposal, with Kushner joining by video; and Kushner “very directly” demanded that Ukraine stop striking russian oil refineries — Zelensky is willing if russia reciprocates. According to the Kyiv Independent, citing the New York Times, the release of US citizen Stephen Hubbard may also be discussed. There is no text of the proposal and no official readout from Oslo.
Trump–Xi–Putin summit — a reminder from 19 October. According to Axios (Barak Ravid), Trump wants a three-way meeting with the leaders of China and russia in China next month, probably on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen in mid-November, to talk about denuclearisation, “not so much for Ukraine”. The Kremlin has floated the idea since July, and Putin raised it in two calls with Trump; Beijing has not signalled readiness for such a summit (per Axios), and China’s Foreign Ministry has not confirmed it, according to an Ukrainska Pravda headline (19.10).
Другий день поспіль Трамп звинувачує Зел: For a second day running, Trump put the onus on Zelensky. In the Oval Office on 20 October he told reporters: “Zelenskyy has to want to settle this war … if he doesn’t, I think it’s going to be a very bad thing” (Fox News live blog). He called the “hatred” between Putin and Zelensky the main obstacle, said the US and Europe have got “nothing but grief, death and huge losses of money”, and said Zelensky “could have made a much better deal” at the time of their Oval Office row two years ago. According to Gordon (20.10 22:58), he also put US aid at $350 billion without explaining the figure; we have not verified it. On 19 October, on Truth Social, Trump had already accused Zelensky of not wanting to end the war.
Рубіо і Зеленський. У 45-хвилинній розмо: Rubio and Zelensky. In a 45-minute call, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio assured Zelensky that no one had ordered curbs on intelligence-sharing or supplies: “No change was ordered. It is not true that we restricted it.” (Axios, Barak Ravid, 20.10). He did, however, acknowledge that Patriot systems paid for by NATO allies could be delayed because they are needed to protect US bases, and called missed warnings of russian ballistic missile strikes technical glitches. Zelensky wrote on X that the situation with Starlink and its military counterpart Starshield “needs to be restored”. Two days earlier (NBC, 18.10) Zelensky had spoken of intelligence-sharing being resumed — see Source divergences.
Кремль дякує посередникам і мовчить про: The Kremlin thanks the mediators and says nothing about Donbas. Putin’s spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on 20 October (per The Moscow Times) that the Kremlin hoped to arrange a meeting with Witkoff “in the near future” so that he could brief Putin on his contacts with the Ukrainian and European sides; Peskov expressed “great gratitude” to the American negotiators for their mediation and said Moscow wanted to continue exchanging views on a number of “very important issues”. He did not mention Moscow’s demands on Donbas. According to Axios and the Kyiv Independent, that meeting is set for 21 October.

Після розмови Путіна з Віткоффом 21 жовт: Hours after Putin met Donald Trump’s envoy Steve Witkoff on 21 October, the kremlin said it was ready “in principle” to resume three-way talks with the US and Ukraine in November, and russia freed an American, Stephen Hubbard. No date or format has been agreed; according to Axios, Putin’s only concession so far is agreeing to talk. The same night russia launched 210 drones and missiles at Ukraine, including ballistic missiles on Kyiv — 1 killed and 22 wounded (State Emergency Service) — and hits were recorded at 32 locations nationwide, the most since at least 3 October.
Кремль «в принципі» готовий до переговор: kremlin “in principle” ready for talks with the US and Ukraine in November
росія «в принципі» готова відновити трис: russia is ready “in principle” to resume three-way talks with the US and Ukraine “around the tenth of November”, Yuri Ushakov, Putin’s foreign-policy aide, said after a roughly three-hour meeting between Putin and US special envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg on 21 October (Ukrinform, citing Fontanka, 21.10 17:10); Jared Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law, joined by video (Axios). Abu Dhabi is a possible venue; a US official told Axios that both Kyiv, at talks in Oslo, and Moscow had accepted a technical meeting in this format. russia also released Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old American. No date or format has been officially confirmed; Axios’s assessment is that Putin’s only concession so far is agreeing to negotiate.

Київ, ніч на 22 жовтня — за кілька годин: Kyiv, night of 22 October — a few hours after the kremlin said it was ready to talk. russia struck the capital with ballistic missiles in three waves: around 22:00 on 21.10, at 02:00 and at 03:00 (Ukraine’s Air Force, Kyiv City Military Administration). According to the State Emergency Service as of 07:55, 1 person was killed (Dniprovskyi district) and 22 wounded, including 4 children. By district: Pecherskyi — 8 (including 3 children), Holosiivskyi — 6, Dniprovskyi — 5 plus a child in hospital, Obolonskyi — 2. In Pecherskyi, the central district that is home to the government quarter, 18 residential buildings on 5 streets were damaged, as were an ambulance station, six ambulances and the facade and windows of the St Vvedensky Monastery; in Sviatoshynskyi district a restaurant complex caught fire (1,100 sq m, the fire was put out). The Southern Bridge over the Dnipro was closed to traffic from the right bank to the left, and the green metro line ran a limited service. The figures may rise.

Серпухов (Московська область), ніч на 22: Serpukhov (Moscow region, about 100 km south of Moscow), night of 22 October. Drones attacked the 75th arsenal of russia’s MoD, which stores and repairs weapons, including air-defence systems; the Telegram channel Astra geolocated video of an explosion to military unit 42708, and local residents reported powerful blasts (NV, 07:36 22.10). The damage has not been assessed; there is no official confirmation from Ukraine’s General Staff, the SBU or HUR (military intelligence) in the materials read. Local authorities have said nothing about Serpukhov: Moscow mayor Sergei Sobyanin reported hundreds of drones destroyed over the capital region (163 by 04:30 per Lenta.ru; 630 between 20:30 and 04:00 per NV), but not this site. Verdict: the strike is not officially confirmed, and local authorities are silent about the site.

Нестача ракет до Patriot і обмеження Sta: Ukraine’s shortage of Patriot missiles and the limits on Starshield, SpaceX’s military satellite service, remain a vulnerability. According to the Kyiv Independent (21.10), Defence Minister Yevhen Khmara and Commander-in-Chief Mykhailo Drapatyi met a Lockheed Martin delegation about increasing deliveries of PAC-3 interceptors amid a “serious shortage”. Путін і Віткофф, Санкт-Петербург, 21 жов: Putin and Witkoff, St Petersburg, 21 October. According to Axios, the meeting lasted about three hours, with Kushner joining by video; Witkoff presented an updated proposal for ending the war. Putin announced the release of US citizen Stephen Hubbard, 74, who had spent more than four years in russian captivity after being detained in Ukraine in 2022. Ushakov said russia was ready “in principle” to resume three-way talks “around the tenth of November”, possibly in Abu Dhabi (Axios), with a post-war security system for russia and Ukraine as the main topic; he claimed that a meeting planned after the State Duma elections had been derailed by a Ukrainian strike on polling day (BBC Russian, Ukrinform; unverified). A US official (Axios) said Ukraine had accepted a technical three-way meeting in Oslo, and russia in St Petersburg. Putin also offered to mediate between the US and Iran and wants to discuss a meeting with Trump in China in mid-November (Axios). Witkoff called Putin a “humanist”; Senators Thom Tillis and John Cornyn publicly criticised him for it. There is no official readout and no date for the talks.
Осло, 20 жовтня — коротко, докладно в по: Oslo, 20 October — in brief; full account in the previous issue. Witkoff discussed a single “framework agreement” to end the war with Zelensky, the leaders of Norway and Finland, and representatives of France, the UK, Germany, Poland, the EU and NATO; a US official (Axios) spoke of “significant progress”. Zelensky sees a three-way meeting with Putin and Trump as the next step — a format russia has so far rejected.

Ukraine’s human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets and russia’s MoD confirmed the start; according to the White House, the truce was brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump. Right after 03:00 russia struck Kyiv with ballistic missiles: a 46-year-old woman was killed and 14 people were wounded (Mayor Vitali Klitschko, National Police). The ceasefire’s duration and terms have not been published, and it is unclear whether it will hold.

Зустріч Зеленського й Путіна «буде орган: A meeting between Volodymyr Zelensky and Vladimir Putin will be set up “very soon”, and “a lot of progress” is being made on russia–Ukraine, Donald Trump told reporters on 28 October after landing at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland (Kyiv Post, 07:21). He named no date or venue, and neither Kyiv nor Moscow has publicly confirmed that the two leaders have agreed to meet; on 25.10 Trump had promised trilateral talks “very soon” too (according to CGTN). Moscow sounds cooler: on 27 October Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said only that the date of the trilateral talks would be announced “in due course”, and Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said the war “tends to escalate”.
